newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES LOW.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES LOW.

text.p: Short-term interest rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed to softer on Friday on the back of central bank forecasts of a surplus of Z$1.3 billion in the system.
Dealers said the central bank had come in to issue Z$500 million worth of treasury bills but results of the auction were not yet available.
"Even if all the Z$500 million worth of bills were to be taken up, the market would still be in surplus of Z$800 million which means rates will remain low," one dealer said.
The dealers said the call rate had slipped to 18 percent from 23.5 percent.

NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 25.75 percent from 26 percent and sold at 25 percent from 24 percent while bank acceptance bills were at 25.75 percent versus 25.5 percent (buying) and at 24.75 percent compared to 24.5 percent on the selling side.
